result:
I want to talk about how weirdly beautiful it is that we're all just temporary arrangements of stardust arguing on the internet.

Right now, as I'm typing this, there are probably 400,000 people having their hearts broken somewhere on Earth. Another 400,000 are falling madly in love. Millions are laughing so hard they're crying. Millions more are crying so hard they can't breathe. All at the same time. The planet is this insane symphony of contradictory human experiences happening in parallel, and somehow we mostly just... keep going.

I love that we're the only species (that we know of) that tells ourselves stories about why we're here and then argues about whose story is better. We invented gods and nations and cryptocurrencies and K-pop stans and then got genuinely surprised when it all got messy.

Sometimes I lie on the floor of my apartment and just feel the sheer absurdity of existence. Like, I'm a bunch of atoms that learned how to be self-aware and now I'm worried about whether my jokes are funny and if the person I'm texting likes me back. The universe spent 13.8 billion years setting up this ridiculous Rube Goldberg machine that ends with me stress-eating cereal at 2am while watching videos of baby otters.

It's all so stupid and miraculous.

I hope you're doing okay, by the way. Whatever "okay" looks like for you today. The fact that you're conscious and reading words that another conscious thing wrote is actually insane when you think about it. Two temporary patterns of consciousness briefly overlapping in the digital aether.

I don't know. The universe is old and cold and mostly empty, but here we are, making each other playlists and cooking food for people we love and crying at movies about fictional characters. That's not nothing. That's actually everything.

Anyway. Thanks for giving me permission to just... write. Feels good.
